cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental course, principle, or path that can be followed or articulated.
cards.Nuance (English): Often refers to the ultimate Way rather than an ordinary road.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter words or state something verbally.
cards.Nuance (English): Common in early literary Chinese, where the same form can also mean a noun.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The ruler does not speak.|The Master states the matter.|Everyone speaks of it.|I do not dare speak it.
cards.Sentences: 君不道。|子道其事。|人皆道之。|吾不敢道。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expressing possibility, capability, or permissibility.
cards.Nuance (English): Marks potential or permissive force rather than completed action.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative marker that denies or reverses the following predicate or relation.
cards.Nuance (English): In this text it introduces contrastive negation rather than simple rejection.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Being mistaken, incorrect, or not right.
cards.Nuance (English): Used predicatively to judge a thing or statement as incorrect.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese
cards.Sentence Translations (English): This is not right.|Its speech is wrong.|Right and wrong are not yet settled.|The Way is not trivial.
cards.Sentences: 此非也。|其言非。|是非未定。|道非小。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Way; the stable principle that does not vary.
cards.Nuance (English): Denotes a permanent principle, not a temporary or ordinary path.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The word, title, or designation by which something is called or identified.
cards.Nuance (English): In this passage it contrasts with the nameless source behind things.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give something a name or call it by a designation.
cards.Nuance (English): Often takes an object and may be followed by the resulting name.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Later people named it.|The people name the mountain.|Confucius named it.|The minister names the vessel.
cards.Sentences: 後人名之。|眾人名山。|孔子名之。|臣名其器。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed, enduring designation that does not change.
cards.Nuance (English): Suggests a name that is stable and not contingent or temporary.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates absence of something, or a state in which something is not present.
cards.Nuance (English): Here it forms a privative expression, not a substantive philosophical noun.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Nameless, it is the beginning of heaven and earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Nonbeing or complete absence, treated as a substantive philosophical concept.
cards.Nuance (English): Abstract and philosophical, especially common in Laozi-style discourse.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): All things are born from nothingness.|The sage holds to nothingness.|Nothingness arises from stillness.|The Way is rooted in nothingness.
cards.Sentences: 萬物生於無。|聖人守無。|無生於靜。|道本於無。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired cosmic realms of heaven and earth; the whole ordered world.
cards.Nuance (English): A fixed cosmological pair, not two separate ordinary objects.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Nameless, it is the beginning of heaven and earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A structural or possessive particle linking a noun modifier to what follows.
cards.Nuance (English): Marks a noun relation rather than carrying independent lexical content.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Nameless, it is the beginning of heaven and earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person object pronoun referring back to a previously mentioned person or thing.
cards.Nuance (English): Common in early literary Chinese as a direct object or resumed object.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese
cards.Sentence Translations (English): I see it.|The people love it.|The ruler uses it.|You know it.
cards.Sentences: 吾見之。|民愛之。|王用之。|子知之。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The first stage, onset, or origin of something.
cards.Nuance (English): Refers to origin in time or sequence, not merely a starting point in space.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially philosophical Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Nameless, it is the beginning of heaven and earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To start an action, process, or state.
cards.Nuance (English): Used for the onset of an event or activity.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Spring begins to grow.|The ruler begins to listen.|The people begin to know.|The Way begins to become clear.
cards.Sentences: 春始生。|君始聽。|民始知。|道始明。
